 France's No. 1 couldn't extend his run in front of his home crowd. Outplayed in every department, he fell to the American, who still has a shot at qualifying for the Turin Finals.
 Taylor Fritz at the 2024 US Open semifinals. © DIMITAR DILKOFF / AFP Jules Hypolite 05/11/2026, 19:34 2 min to read Follow us ATP Masters 1000 Fils Fritz Paris And that makes three for the United States. After the eliminations of Quentin Halys and Arthur Rinderknech against Americans this Thursday (Paul and Shelton), it was Arthur Fils' turn to fall tonight.
 Less than 24 hours after defeating Tomas Machac in front of the Plenitude Arena crowd, France's No. 1 returned to center court to take on Taylor Fritz, ranked No. 12 in the world, against whom he had retired last week in Basel .
 Remove ads Fritz Imperious From Start to Finish
 Under the spotlight, Fils struggled throughout the match, completely dominated by the American, who was excellent on the return and able to rely on a serve as devastating as ever (14 aces).
 Very quickly, the former US Open finalist broke serve in the first set, then at the very start of the second, dashing Fils' hopes of a comeback in front of his home fans.
 The Frenchman offered nothing on the return, failing to create a single break point in the entire match. He eventually went down 6-3, 6-4 after just 1 hour and 11 minutes of play.
 Fils Awaits the Finals, Fritz Keeps His Qualification Hopes Alive
 Despite this premature exit in Paris, Arthur Fils can now take time to rest and prepare for the ATP Finals in Turin (November 15-22), the major goal of the end of his season.
 He could well face Taylor Fritz there, as the American is now just two wins away (or one, if Paul doesn't reach the semifinals) from securing the 8th and final spot for the season-ending event.
 But the American will need to pull off a remarkable feat tomorrow against Carlos Alcaraz, who is riding a six-match indoor winning streak, if he wants to book his ticket to Turin and keep his Rolex Paris Masters campaign alive.
